subtitle.en: An original passage on learning, intellectual humility, and changing your mind without losing yourself.
subtitle.zh: 一篇原创美文：关于学习、思想上的谦逊，以及如何改变想法而不失去自我。

note.en: Public-domain inspiration for deliberate self-improvement and more modest language; the passage itself is original.
note.zh: 以公开领域作品中关于主动自我改进与谦逊表达的思想为灵感；正文为原创。

warmup.en: Read with reflective strength. This is not an apology for weakness; it is a defense of honest learning.
warmup.zh: 用沉思而有力量的语气朗读。这不是为软弱辩护，而是在捍卫诚实的学习。

intro.en: This original passage considers revision not as embarrassment, but as one of the mature forms of courage.
intro.zh: 这篇原创文章把“修正”视为一种成熟的勇气，而不是尴尬。

sections.text: There is a special fatigue in needing to be right all the time. Every new fact becomes a threat, every question a test, every disagreement a small public trial. We begin protecting yesterday's opinion as if it were our name. But an opinion is not a home we must defend forever. It is a working map. A good map helps us move; when the landscape proves it wrong, we redraw it. The purpose was never to admire the map. The purpose was to find our way.

coaching.en: Let the first sentence carry weight, then brighten slightly when the map image appears.
coaching.zh: 第一句要有重量；地图意象出现时，语气稍微明亮起来。

sections.text: Certain phrases keep the mind ventilated. As I understand it. Based on what I know now. I may be missing something. These words do not drain authority from a speaker; they show that confidence has a foundation rather than a costume. They also invite useful correction. Compare You are wrong with Here is the part I see differently. The second phrase opens a window. Air enters. More importantly, another person may enter too, carrying evidence we could not have found alone.

coaching.en: Give each modest phrase its own pause. Keep Here is the part I see differently curious, not evasive.
coaching.zh: 每个谦逊表达后都停一下。Here is the part I see differently 要读得好奇，而不是闪躲。

sections.text: Changing your mind can feel awkward because other people witnessed the earlier version. We imagine that consistency will earn more respect than honesty. Often the opposite is true. A clear revision can sound like this: I believed the deadline was flexible. I have now seen the client agreement, and I was mistaken. Here is what I will change. Nothing in that sequence requires self-contempt. It names the old belief, acknowledges the evidence, and moves responsibility forward. Revision becomes credible when it produces a different action.

coaching.en: Read the example plainly, without shame. Stress what I will change and different action.
coaching.zh: 示例要平实，不带羞耻。重读 what I will change 和 different action。

sections.text: We need convictions, but we need them for living, not for display. Hold them firmly enough to act and lightly enough to examine. The strongest mind is not a locked room with thick walls. It is a well-built room with windows: sheltered from every passing gust, yet open to weather, distance, and light. When better evidence arrives, opening a window does not destroy the room. It reveals what the room is for. We are not betraying ourselves when we revise honestly. We are becoming more loyal to the search.

coaching.en: Build the room-and-window image slowly. Finish with warmth on loyal to the search.
coaching.zh: 慢慢建立房间与窗户的意象。最后在 loyal to the search 上温暖收束。

meaning.en: A useful but changeable model for understanding reality.
meaning.zh: 用来理解现实、但可以修正的模型。

use.en: Treat an opinion as a working map.
use.zh: 把观点当作一张可以修订的地图。

meaning.en: Supplied with fresh air; figuratively, kept open to new thought.
meaning.zh: 通风的；比喻思想保持开放。

use.en: Modest language keeps the mind ventilated.
use.zh: 谦逊的语言让头脑保持通透。

meaning.en: The underlying support on which something rests.

use.zh: 真正的自信有坚实基础。

use.en: Revision is credible when action changes.
use.zh: 当行动改变时，修正才可信。

meaning.en: A firmly held belief or principle.
meaning.zh: 坚定持有的信念或原则。

use.en: A conviction should guide action, not decorate identity.
use.zh: 信念应当指导行动，而不是装饰身份。

meaning.en: To be disloyal to a person, value, or trust.

use.en: Honest revision does not betray the self.
use.zh: 诚实的修正并不是背叛自我。

pronunciationFocus.en: Keep the final consonants clear in fact, threat, test, and respect.
pronunciationFocus.zh: 清楚读出 fact, threat, test, respect 的词尾辅音。

pronunciationFocus.en: Use a three-part rhythm for names the old belief, acknowledges the evidence, and moves responsibility forward.
pronunciationFocus.zh: 用三段式节奏朗读 names the old belief, acknowledges the evidence, and moves responsibility forward。

pronunciationFocus.en: Contrast firmly enough to act with lightly enough to examine.
pronunciationFocus.zh: 对比朗读 firmly enough to act 与 lightly enough to examine。

prompt.en: Practice a voice that can admit uncertainty without collapsing into apology.
prompt.zh: 练习一种能够承认不确定、却不会陷入过度道歉的声音。

steps.en: Pass one: copy the pauses in the modest opening phrases.
steps.zh: 第一遍：模仿谦逊开场语中的停顿。

steps.en: Pass two: deliver the revision example with steady responsibility.
steps.zh: 第二遍：以稳定、负责的语气说出修正示例。

steps.en: Pass three: state one belief using Based on what I know now.
steps.zh: 第三遍：用 Based on what I know now 表达一个观点。

reflection.en: Which belief in your life should remain a working map rather than a fixed identity?
reflection.zh: 生活中的哪个观点，应该只是一张可修改的地图，而不是固定身份？

reflection.en: What new evidence would genuinely change your mind?
reflection.zh: 什么样的新证据，真的会让你改变想法？
